agent_rules: Do not record --actor-type human unless the user explicitly approved the specific artifact.
Use --approval-source explicit-user only with a summary or canonical evidence of the user's approval.

By default, a user approval applies only to the artifact or decision just shown and summarized; do not reuse a short approval for future artifacts, templates, capability decisions, contracts, or task start confirmations.

If the user explicitly specifies a broader approval level or autonomy scope, respect that level inside the stated boundaries and record later in-scope formal artifacts with --approval-source automation, --actor-type agent, and a summary/evidence of the delegated approval.
Delegated automation approval must not expand scope to installs, deploys, secrets, external services, destructive commands, or unrelated work without another explicit approval.
Use --approval-source bootstrap only for migration/provisional records; bootstrap approvals do not satisfy strict gates by default.
Treat permission to implement or push as operational authorization, not as formal SDLC approval.
approval_policy.principle: Implementation authorization is not formal SDLC approval. Formal approvals must record an explicit source, approver, summary or evidence, and immutable subject hash. Project policy and approval invariants are recorded together but are not the same thing. formal_approval_requires_explicit_source, require_summary_or_evidence_for_explicit_user, require_summary_or_evidence_for_automation, allow_bootstrap_approvals_in_strict_gate, legacy_approval_behavior, and accepted_sources are read from this file and a project may change them. content_authorization_schema, host_approval_receipt_schema, authorization_usage_receipt_schema, require_proposal_bound_authorization_for_assessments, require_usage_receipt_for_automation, and close_authorization_on_workflow_terminal state what the CLI always does: the three schema names record which shipped schema validates each record, and the three requirements are always enforced. They are recorded so the guarantee is legible, and setting one to false or pointing it elsewhere does not turn the check off. agent_rules is guidance for whoever records an approval, not a switch. An approval rule that a project could relax from inside the project it governs would not be a rule. host_approval_receipt_directory, authorization_usage_receipt_directory and require_host_assurance_for_direct_human_or_ci_approval are not read either; they remain because the effective configuration fills missing keys from the frozen 0.11.0 defaults, which still carry them.

assessment_workflow.principle: A normal assessment has exactly two user checkpoints: canonical project context and one immutable combined proposal. Internal records are applied idempotently after proposal authorization.

autonomy_policy.principle: Autonomy is negotiated per requirement as a ceiling and selected again for every pull request or local release. A downstream delivery, contract, capability, environment, or budget may narrow that level but never widen it. Project policy and autonomy invariants are recorded together but are not the same thing. enabled, mode, storage_root, allowed_levels, default_requirement_ceiling, legacy_default, require_explicit_delivery_selection, delivery_kinds, delivery_providers, presets, exception_triggers, local_release.writes_outside_workspace_require_checkpoint, and local_release.machine_global_changes_require_checkpoint are read from this file and a project may change them. requirement_profile_schema, delivery_profile_schema, delivery_profile_schema_v2, decision_schema, fail_closed_on_unknown, bounded_autonomous_requires_host_verified, every pull_request entry, local_release.require_target_root, and local_release.require_rollback state what the CLI always does: the four schema names record which shipped schema validates each record, an unrecognised level is refused, bounded-autonomous is capped to checkpointed unless authority_policy.mode is host_verified, and a delivery target is always fully identified, never reused for another delivery, and always carries a rollback procedure. They are recorded so the guarantee is legible, and setting one to false or pointing it elsewhere does not turn the check off. An autonomy ceiling that the delivery it authorizes could raise from inside would not be a ceiling. local_release.require_smoke_test is not read: a release may declare no smoke test. It remains because the effective configuration fills missing keys from the frozen 0.11.0 defaults, which still carry it.

budget_policy.principle: Checkpoint 2 approves the work together with its budget. The shipped limits are soft: when usage reaches one, work pauses and you decide whether to extend the budget or stop. Token and cost figures are estimates. Hard limits are optional and need a trusted, signed exact meter (see docs/limits-and-metering.md).

cache_policy.principle: Cache and index files are local, derived, and regenerable optimizations. They can accelerate lookup and context assembly, but they must never be used as the canonical source for approvals, requirements, decisions, or story outputs.

agent_rules: Profile the project or story before technical analysis when the stack, integrations, or useful capabilities are unclear.
Recommend skills, MCPs, tools, models, and bindings from evidence, not from language keywords.

Run `capability inventory` to learn which skills, commands, plugins, and MCP servers are already installed, and `capability recommend --from-inventory` to propose the ones that match the declared stack, instead of asking the user to list them.
Ask for approval before installing missing capabilities or using external/write/production targets.
Apply approved recommendations to contracts instead of duplicating capability decisions in chat.
capability_discovery_policy.principle: Capability discovery is contextual and technology-agnostic. Codex or another LLM proposes canonical profiles and recommendations; the CLI validates, persists, approves, and applies only structured JSON with evidence.

claim_policy.principle: Project policy and claim invariants are recorded together but are not the same thing. require_branch_pattern and default_ttl_seconds are read from this file and a project may change them. one_active_claim_per_story and release_before_reclaim state what the CLI always enforces when a story is claimed: they are recorded so the guarantee is legible, and setting one to false does not turn the check off. Single ownership of a claimed story is what keeps parallel tracks safe, so it cannot be waived from inside the project it protects.

contract_generation.principle: Contract templates are generic. Generated contracts must be contextualized for the target project by inspecting project KB artifacts, reading user-provided files, and asking questions when critical context is missing.

execution_policy.principle: Contracts run inside Codex. If a contract does not explicitly override model or reasoning, spawned agents should inherit the main Codex thread configuration.

gate_policy.principle: Project policy and strict-gate invariants are recorded together but are not the same thing. implementation_requires_claim, implementation_requires_acceptance_criteria, validation_requires_test_trace, release_requires_release_trace, strict_mode.requires_output_contract_coverage, strict_mode.requires_write_scope_integrity, contract_required_fields, and story_required_fields, secret_scan.enabled, secret_scan.rules, secret_scan.exclude_paths, and merge_requires_code_review are read from this file and a project may change them. secret_scan.enabled and merge_requires_code_review are read as an explicit true, so a project that never declared them keeps the gate it agreed to and no plugin update can start blocking its deliveries or merges. merge_requires_code_review set to true refuses every pull_request.merge until an approved code-review:v1 record exists for the exact head being merged, by a reviewer whose actor and Git email differ from every commit author of the pull request; the template sets it to false, so that check applies only to the pull requests whose story the user chose to review, a choice recorded in the approved delivery profile and enforced only at pull_request.merge. Every other strict_mode entry states what --strict always enforces: it is recorded so the guarantee is legible, and setting it to false does not turn the check off. A gate that could be disabled from inside the project it governs would not be a gate.

approval_boundaries.effect_of_answer: It changes the proposal write-set, capability constraints, authorization subjects/actions, and exception triggers.

en: Authorize local reads and writes only to .sdlc/ and docs/assessment.pdf; no installs or production.
it: Autorizzo solo lettura locale e scritture in .sdlc/ e docs/assessment.pdf; niente installazioni o produzione.

approval_boundaries.why_needed: An explicit boundary prevents a short answer from being reused as authority for unseen writes, tools, environments, or future artifacts.

budget_time.effect_of_answer: It updates the immutable execution budget, metering policy, completion reserve, stop action, and amendment boundary.

en: At most 60 minutes of active time; warn at 70% and 90%, reserve 15% for verification.
it: Massimo 60 minuti di tempo attivo; avvisa al 70% e 90%, riserva il 15% alla verifica.

budget_time.why_needed: A concrete, meterable tranche defines warning, reserve, stop, and partial-delivery behavior before work starts.

constraints_nfr.effect_of_answer: It updates explicit constraints, risk severity, architecture options, acceptance criteria, and excluded approaches.

en: EU data residency, 99.9% availability, and no migration downtime.
it: Dati in UE, disponibilità 99,9%, nessun downtime durante la migrazione.

constraints_nfr.why_needed: Constraints and non-functional requirements are architectural boundaries; omitting them can reverse a recommendation.

integrations.effect_of_answer: It updates the component boundary, evidence sources, access policy, risks, and any exceptional authorization needed.

en: Assess Stripe and Salesforce from local documentation only; do not access the tenants.
it: Considera Stripe e Salesforce solo dalla documentazione locale; non accedere ai tenant.

integrations.why_needed: Integrations define system boundaries and may require separate credentials, external access, or production approval.

objective.effect_of_answer: It updates the assessment objective, scope emphasis, acceptance criteria, and intended decision in checkpoint 2.

en: The objective is to decide whether to modernize the architecture in the next six months.
it: L'obiettivo è decidere se modernizzare l'architettura nei prossimi sei mesi.

objective.why_needed: The objective determines which evidence and recommendations are decision-relevant and prevents a generic assessment.

output_delivery.effect_of_answer: It changes the canonical artifact metadata, generator capability, render evidence, output path, and verification plan.

en: Deliver a DOCX at docs/assessment.docx plus a short chat summary.
it: Consegna un DOCX in docs/assessment.docx più un riepilogo breve in chat.

output_delivery.why_needed: The requested format and destination select the real generator, verification dimensions, artifact path, and delivery mode.

users_stakeholders.effect_of_answer: It changes the audience, explanation depth, decision framing, and stakeholder-specific recommendations.

en: The document is for the CTO, platform team, and security owner.
it: Il documento è per CTO, team platform e responsabile sicurezza.

users_stakeholders.why_needed: Audience and stakeholder needs determine terminology, depth, prioritization, and which trade-offs must be made explicit.

fallback.does_not_authorize: Answering an open question does not authorize execution, writes, external access, production access, or additional budget unless those boundaries are displayed in the proposal.
fallback.effect_of_answer: The answer is recorded in the relevant scope, assumption, or delivery field; a material change after approval creates a new proposal hash.

en: It is not decided yet: use the stated assumption and record the limitation.
it: Non è ancora deciso: usa l'ipotesi indicata e segnala il limite.

fallback.why_needed: The answer replaces an unstated assumption with an explicit, reviewable proposal input.

certification_drift.principle: A story's final certification binds the exact content it certified: its records, the files in its requirement write paths, and its release targets. 1. A story's own records never change: its contract, requirements and profiles, workflow records, test and story records, and output registry entry must stay as certified; delivery execution and related governance records may only gain files, story records only under base-acknowledgements/, and its trace only autonomy delivery reconcile events whose chain still verifies. Any other change voids the receipt. 2. Shared files (project, configuration, referenced governance, write-path files, release targets) changed later by others make the certification stale. With mode stale a stale story stays completed only once its delivery finished: a pull request merged or acknowledged with autonomy delivery reconcile, or a local release closed as released; before that it is blocked. With reopen any change blocks it, as in earlier versions. 3. A merged pull-request story is certified on its merge commit, which must be in the clone and an ancestor of HEAD; work merged after it is never charged to it. 4. A certified commit missing from the clone or no longer an ancestor of HEAD is reported as such and never counts as stale. The receipt's own identity (its hash, workflow, checkpoint, and task start) must always verify, and records are never rewritten.

claim_activity.principle: There is no heartbeat: a claim's last sign of life is read from git. With mode git, status and orchestrate status show, for each claim held on another computer, the last commit on the claim's branch as the remote has it (after status_sync) and how many commits it is ahead of the base branch. idle_after_seconds marks a claim idle when that last commit is older; it is only a notice and never frees the story (that stays stale_claim_after_seconds and the claim's expiry). null never marks a claim idle; off turns the check off.

claim_identity.principle: A shared claim is an immutable record every reader of the remote sees, so beyond the agent label it records who made it only when the project opts in. git_user true adds the git user.name of the claiming computer. host_label_env names an environment variable each computer may set to a label of its choice (the host name is never read); when it is set, the label is added. Both are shown by status and orchestrate status next to the agent.

delivered_overlap.principle: Stories started from the same project state can both change one area. When another story's merged delivery changed a file inside this story's write scope after this story started, write_scope decides what happens before this story merges: confirm requires an overlap review (story overlap confirm) that names each such change, warn only reports it, off ignores it. context applies the same choice to files this story only read. confirmation_actor any lets the agent working on the story record the review; human requires a person. claim warn lists other stories in progress whose write scope overlaps when a story is claimed; it never blocks a claim.

merge_drift.principle: Story records move only through recorded lifecycle steps, so work merged by hand, or by an agent that stopped before recording completion, leaves a story open. status reports open stories whose work is already on the remote base branch, read from git only after status_sync: a first-parent commit that merges one of the story's branches or, when match_commit_subject is true, whose subject names the story id. Commits that change only project records and reverts never count. It never changes a record. base_branch null means the remote's default branch; max_commits_scanned bounds the history read; off turns the check off.

orchestration_policy.principle: Parallel work across several computers is safe only when every computer sees the same story claims. coordination decides where claims are recorded: auto shares them through this git remote when it exists and keeps them on this computer otherwise; required refuses to claim without the remote; local_only never shares them, for a project worked on from one computer only. A shared claim is created on the remote before the claim file, and when sharing applies and the remote cannot be reached, story claim is refused, because claiming is the start of work. Releases, handoffs, and closures publish a release record so the story can be claimed again; taking over a claim held elsewhere is a person's decision, recorded on the remote for the previous holder to see. stale_claim_after_seconds lists a claim as stale in orchestrate status once it is that old, even before it expires; null means only its expiry counts. status_list_limit bounds how many stories or records status names in each of its lists (ready, blocked, records to refresh, merged but still open).

reservation.principle: story reserve books a story before it can start (for example while its dependencies are not satisfied yet), through the same create-only refs on the git remote as claims. It needs no task start, writes nothing in the project, and fixes no starting point. Other computers see who reserved it and until when, and their story claim is refused unless a person takes it over with --force and --reason. story claim from the reserving computer turns the reservation into the claim. A reservation always expires: default_expires_in_seconds applies when no --expires-in or --expires-at is given, max_expires_in_seconds is the longest allowed; an expired reservation ends by itself, and story release ends it earlier.

status_sync.principle: status first brings this clone up to date, so it reports what other computers merged. fetch updates only the remote-tracking branches and never changes files; pull also fast-forwards the current branch when it is strictly behind its upstream and git can do so without touching local changes; off reads the clone as it is. A remote that cannot be reached is a warning, never an error. The remote is the current branch's own remote, or coordination.remote.

unclaimed_remote_work.principle: A claim is shared from the story's task start on, so work begun earlier is invisible to other computers. With mode git, status, orchestrate status, and story availability warn when a story nobody claimed or reserved already has a branch on the remote that names it with commits not yet on the base branch. pull_requests github-cli also reads open pull requests through the GitHub CLI when it is installed and signed in; off reads git only. recent_within_seconds ignores branches whose last commit is older; null counts any age. It only warns and never changes a record; off turns it off.

workflow_history.principle: Every computer appends workflow audit records to the one shared project history (.sdlc/traces/project.jsonl), which is a single hash chain. When records written on several computers are copied onto one branch afterwards, that chain no longer verifies as a whole even though each workflow's own records are intact. With check workflow, status and the other read-only lifecycle views verify each story workflow on its own chained records and report the divergence; with project they also require the whole history to verify first, so every story workflow is blocked while it does not. Writes and trace verify always check the whole history. With divergence warn, status and doctor compare this clone's project history with the remote base branch's and, when the two have forked, warn before publishing with the events only on each side; trace rebase --onto <remote>/<branch> --apply moves this clone's own events after the other branch's history and keeps their original fingerprints. off turns the warning off.

agent_rules: Read the output registry before producing an artifact.
Resolve the artifact type for the story and requirement.
Prefer reuse plus delta when another story already covers the same requirement.
Ask the user before introducing a new template or changing an approved output structure.
Link every durable output to story, requirement, artifact path, template id, and reuse mode.
output_consistency_policy.principle: Every durable story output should resolve an approved project-wide output template before generation. Related stories should reuse the approved base artifact and create only an explicit delta unless the user approves a new structure.

parallel_work.principle: Parallel work is story-scoped. Each active story lane has one active claim, an auditable actor, a branch, trace events, and explicit release or handoff.
parallel_work.stale_claim_policy: expired active claims block implementation until released, renewed, or force-reclaimed by a human

analysis.purpose: Translate approved discovery output into functional and technical analysis with integrations, APIs, mocks, and system boundaries.
validation: user flows include inputs and outputs

design.purpose: Convert analysis into user stories, task decomposition, acceptance criteria, test strategy, and UX or architecture decisions.
validation: test strategy maps to acceptance criteria

discovery.purpose: Understand the problem, target users, market context, constraints, and value hypothesis before solution design.
validation: feature proposal links to user value

implementation.purpose: Implement story-scoped changes on dedicated branches using the approved contract, tests, and knowledge base context.
validation: decision and assumption changes are recorded
no unauthorized tool or resource use

operations.purpose: Track incidents and feedback observed against the released change, keeping the release phase's observability plan and feedback loop populated with real evidence.
validation: each incident record is bound to a released manifest
each feedback record is bound to a released manifest

release.purpose: Package the validated work with documentation, observability, feedback loop, and updated project context.
validation: deployment notes include rollback or recovery path

validation.purpose: Validate implementation against contracts, acceptance criteria, tests, observability needs, and release readiness.
validation: known risks are accepted or mitigated

routing_policy.principle: The route router is language-agnostic. It consumes canonical intent JSON normalized by an LLM or Codex and never classifies raw text with linguistic keywords.

coordination.principle: Slots a standing approval has used and its revocation are also recorded as refs on this git remote, so every clone of the project sees them before it relies on the standing approval. auto shares them when the remote exists and keeps them on this computer otherwise; required refuses to rely on a standing approval without the remote; local_only never shares them. When sharing applies and the remote cannot be reached, the standing approval covers nothing and every step asks for the normal confirmation.

standing_approval_policy.principle: A standing approval is a user-approved, bounded, revocable delegation that lets repeated low-risk deliveries proceed without a confirmation for each one. enabled, max_validity_days, max_deliveries, max_changed_files, max_changed_lines, and expiry_warning_hours are read from this file and a project may change them; they cap what any standing approval may request. What a standing approval may never cover (merge, production, deploy, data migrations, force-push, deletions of tracked files outside its paths) and that it covers only the middle working level are fixed by the CLI and recorded on every standing approval.

trace_policy.principle: Every durable event must be attributable to a human, agent, system, or CI actor. require_actor is read from this file and a project may change it. record_git_metadata, record_run_metadata, and sync_events state what the CLI always records and which sync events it accepts: they are recorded so the guarantee is legible, and setting one to false does not turn the check off. A trace whose git and run provenance could be dropped from inside the project would not be evidence.

verification_policy.principle: Verification claims are dimensioned; container validity never implies semantic or rendered correctness.

work_breakdown_policy.principle: Work breakdown is agreed with the user and stored in .sdlc. Story remains the main delivery and strict-gate unit; epic and task are optional internal aggregation/operational levels.
